rapidShutdown.headline: Projoy Rapid Shutdown
rapidShutdown.subhead: The safety layer that de-energizes PV strings at the panel level within seconds — protecting firefighters, satisfying insurers, and meeting the codes arriving in Thailand now.
rapidShutdown.whyBody: NEC 2017 §690.12 and IEC 60947-3 require module-level shutdown on rooftop PV systems. Rapid Shutdown devices cut string voltage to safe levels within 30 seconds of activation, enabling first responders to work on a roof without risk of electrocution.
rapidShutdown.diagramIntro: Trigger a simulated shutdown to watch the signal travel from the Control Box to each PEFS unit and de-energize the array.

diagram.statusShutdown: Shutdown initiated · Signal sent to PEFS

rapidShutdown.ctaHeading: Need rapid shutdown for your project?

firefighterSwitches.headline: Firefighter Safety Switches
firefighterSwitches.subhead: Dedicated disconnects that let first responders isolate a PV system from outside the building — reducing arc-flash exposure and giving emergency crews full control before they enter a structure.
firefighterSwitches.whyBody: Standard overcurrent protection was not designed for emergency scenarios. Firefighter Safety Switches provide a clearly marked, externally accessible point of disconnection rated for the fault currents found in commercial and industrial PV systems — a requirement increasingly cited in Thai fire safety and insurance frameworks.
firefighterSwitches.diagramIntro: The disconnect lives outside the building envelope so emergency crews can isolate the array before entry — no need to reach the inverter or roof.
firefighterSwitches.ctaHeading: Specify a firefighter switch for your project?
firefighterSwitches.ctaBody: Tell us your system size and installation type and we'll recommend the right disconnect and help with documentation.

whySafety.headline: Why Solar Safety Matters
whySafety.subhead: An energized rooftop PV array presents real hazards — to installers, to building occupants, and to the first responders who arrive when something goes wrong.
whySafety.riskHeading: The risk: voltage that doesn't switch off
whySafety.riskBody: A solar array generates up to 1,000 V DC as long as light is present. Unlike AC mains, conventional breakers and fuses cannot interrupt DC arc faults. A 600 V DC arc can sustain at distances that would extinguish a 240 V AC arc — with temperatures exceeding 20,000 °C. Firefighters entering a burning building with an active rooftop PV system face electrocution, arc-flash, and arc-blast risks with no simple way to de-energize the system.
whySafety.regulationBody: NEC 2017 Section 690.12 requires all conductors on a rooftop to be reduced to 30 V or less within 30 seconds of system shutdown. IEC 60947-3 sets isolation requirements for load-break switches used in PV disconnection applications. Thailand's EGAT and DOE guidelines are aligning with these international frameworks, and insurers are already demanding compliance documentation on commercial projects.
whySafety.wsAnswerHeading: The WS Energy answer: Projoy Rapid Shutdown (exclusive in Thailand)
whySafety.wsAnswerBody: WS Energy is the exclusive authorized distributor of the Projoy Rapid Shutdown family in Thailand. Projoy devices meet NEC §690.12 and IEC 60947-3, carry TIS and UL marks, and are engineered for the string voltages used in Thai C&I and utility-scale installations. Every product in the range ships with authorization documentation your insurer and AHJ will accept.
whySafety.ctaHeading: Ready to make your installation safe and compliant?
whySafety.ctaBody: Talk to a WS Energy sales engineer — we'll spec the right Rapid Shutdown or Firefighter Switch combination for your project and provide the compliance paperwork.
